title: Isolation-based Spherical Ensemble Representations for Tabular Anomaly Detection
summary: Unsupervised tabular anomaly detection faces challenges including conflicting distributional assumptions, computational inefficiency, and difficulty handling diverse anomaly types. The paper proposes ISER, which uses hypersphere radii as a monotonic transformation of local density through ensemble representations, with average-based and similarity-based scoring mechanisms, and extends Isolation Forest to ISER-IF by applying it to the transformed feature space. Comprehensive experiments on 20 real-world datasets demonstrate ISER's competitive performance over 12 SOTA methods, with ISER-S achieving the highest average AUC-ROC of 0.8523 and ISER-IF showing substantial improvements over iForest.

requirements.stmt: Implement hypersphere-based space partitioning by randomly sampling ψ points without replacement for each partitioning
requirements.quote: For each partitioning Hi, we begin by randomly sampling a subset Di ⊂ D of size ψ without replacement

requirements.stmt: Compute hypersphere radius as nearest neighbor distance within sampled subset: r[z] = min_{z'∈Di\{z}} ||z - z'||
requirements.quote: The radius of this hypersphere is determined by the distance between z and its nearest neighbor in Di \ {z}: r[z] = min_{z'∈Di\{z}} ||z - z'||

requirements.stmt: Compute ensemble representation φi(x) = 1 - 1/r[ẑ_i(x)] if covered by any hypersphere, else 1
Construct ensemble representation Φ(x) by concatenating φi(x) across all t partitionings
requirements.quote: The ensemble representation of point x is constructed by concatenating the coverage indicators from all t partitionings

requirements.stmt: Implement average-based scoring Savg(x) = (1/t) Σ_{i=1}^t Φi(x)
requirements.quote: The average-based anomaly score is computed as the arithmetic mean of all ensemble components

requirements.stmt: Implement similarity-based scoring Ssim(x) using cosine similarity between Φ(x) and reference vector 1 = [1,1,...,1]
requirements.quote: The similarity-based anomaly score is computed using cosine similarity between the point's ensemble representation and the anomaly reference vector

requirements.stmt: For ISER-IF, apply iForest to transformed feature space Φ(x) with modified scoring function
requirements.quote: we apply iForest to the transformed feature space Φ(x)

requirements.stmt: Use modified ISER-IF scoring: S_ISER-IF(x,n) = 1 - 2^{-E(h(Φ(x)))/c(n)} where shorter path lengths indicate normal points
requirements.quote: To accommodate this inversion, we modify the original iForest anomaly scoring function [11] as: SISER-IF(x, n) = 1 − 2−E(h(Φ(x)))/c(n)

requirements.stmt: Use hyperparameters t=200 partitionings and ψ ∈ {2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16}
requirements.quote: For iForest, iNNE, IDK, ADERH and proposed methods, ψ ∈{2m, m = 1, 2, . . . , 8} and with default t = 200.

requirements.stmt: Train on entire contaminated dataset (unsupervised setting with both normal and anomalous instances)
requirements.quote: our experiments assume access to the entire dataset containing both normal and anomalous instances during training

requirements.stmt: Evaluate using AUC-ROC metric, averaging over 5 repeated runs
requirements.quote: We use Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC-ROC) as evaluation metrics. Each experiment is repeated 5 times and reported average results.
